findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes with TypeError on the datetime ordering the endpoint uses
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint wires this paginator in with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, "datetime"), which is a datetime object. math.floor/math.ceil raise TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime (DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes to epoch-millis first). build_cursor calls get_item_key(results[0]) via _build_next_values/_build_prev_values, so any request to GET /organizations/{slug}/audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true from an authorized admin 500s on the very first page as soon as the queryset returns a row. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting the epoch-ms cursor back into a datetime, so even a numeric cursor would be compared against a datetime column on subsequent pages. The entire 'optimized' path is unusable as shipped.

findings.title: Unconditional organization_context.member.has_global_access dereferences a member that can be None
findings.body: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None whenever the request is not tied to an organization membership, e.g. legacy API-key or org-token authentication against this endpoint, which previously worked. The new line computes enable_advanced on every GET request, even when optimized_pagination is not passed, and the short-circuit only protects requests where request.user.is_superuser is True. Any non-superuser request with member=None raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access', turning previously successful responses into 500s. The check needs to guard against member being None (e.g. organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access).

findings.title: "Advanced" negative-offset branch 500s: Django forbids negative queryset slicing
findings.body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result branch for enable_advanced_features with cursor.offset < 0 passes the negative offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. The comment claims "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", which is false: QuerySet.__getitem__ asserts "Negative indexing is not supported". Cursor offsets come directly from the user-supplied cursor string (Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no sign validation), so any caller who reaches the optimized path can send cursor=0:-1:0 and trigger an uncaught AssertionError -> 500. The same applies to 0:-1:1 since the branch does not check is_prev. Negative offsets must be rejected with BadPaginationError (which Endpoint.paginate converts to a 400) rather than passed to the ORM.

findings.title: BasePaginator change makes negative cursor offsets silently return page one for forward cursors while prev cursors still 500
findings.body: The changed slicing in BasePaginator.get_result uses start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. A crafted forward cursor with a negative offset (e.g. 0:-5:0) is now silently clamped to 0 and returns the first page instead of being rejected, while a prev cursor with a negative offset (0:-5:1) still reaches the queryset slice and raises Django's uncaught AssertionError "Negative indexing is not supported" -> 500. The added comment ("the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is incorrect for the is_prev case, and the two directions now handle malformed cursors inconsistently. Negative offsets should be validated and rejected with BadPaginationError for both directions instead of clamped or passed through.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator, the negative-offset path, or the endpoint's optimized branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new OptimizedCursorPaginator class, a user-reachable branch in the audit log endpoint, and a behavioral change to BasePaginator.get_result that affects all cursor-paginated endpoints, but adds no tests. Both new code paths fail on first use (the datetime TypeError in get_item_key and the negative-slice AssertionError), which a single happy-path test of GET /organizations/{slug}/audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true would have caught, and the BasePaginator change has no coverage for prev/negative-offset cursors either.

findings.title: New Cursor comment falsely advertises negative offsets as a supported pagination feature
findings.body: The added comment claims negative offsets are allowed "for advanced pagination scenarios" and "enable efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets", but nothing in Cursor changed (int(offset) always accepted negatives), and the paginators that consume offsets either explicitly reject negatives (OffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator, CombinedQuerysetPaginator raise BadPaginationError on negative offsets) or crash on them (Django disallows negative queryset slicing). This documents a contract the rest of the pagination code does not support and could mislead future callers into emitting negative-offset cursors.
